name: Atacama Desert (Yungay Basin)
terrain: Hyper-arid desert plateau and salar flats
geology: Nitrate-perchlorate evaporite crusts, volcanic ignimbrites, hyper-desiccated clay
surface_conditions: Fine oxidized dust, gypsum hardpans, high solar UV irradiance
explanation: DEMO DATA: Represents hyper-arid, oxidized soils and high UV flux comparable to dry Martian basins and ancient lacustrine sediments like Jezero Crater.

name: McMurdo Dry Valleys
terrain: Polar cold desert valley with permafrost
geology: Patterned permafrost ground, cryogenic salts, sandstone and dolerite bedrock
surface_conditions: Snow-free frozen regolith, gravel lag deposits, ice-cemented permafrost
recommended_missions: Lunar South Pole Cold Trap Operations
explanation: DEMO DATA: Models cryogenic soil dynamics, absence of liquid water, and extreme sub-zero thermal stresses characteristic of Lunar South Pole cold traps (PSRs).

name: Devon Island (Haughton Impact Crater)
terrain: Impact crater floor, peak-ring breccia, and periglacial valleys
geology: Impact breccia, hydrothermal paleospring deposits, shatter cones, dolomite bedrock
surface_conditions: Angular shatter blocks, frost-shattered scree, degraded paleolake beds
recommended_missions: Astronaut EVA Navigation and Geologic Traverse Drills
explanation: DEMO DATA: Features a preserved 23-km impact structure with breccia blankets, serving as a topological testbed for lunar and Martian impact craters.

name: Lanzarote Volcanic Fields & Tubes
terrain: Pristine basaltic 'a'a and pahoehoe lava flows and collapse pits
geology: Tholeiitic and alkali olivine basalts, volcanic hornitos, pristine lava tubes
surface_conditions: Abrasive vesicular basalt, unweathered volcanic glass crusts, cave skylights
recommended_missions: Basalt ISRU Sintering and 3D Construction Trials
explanation: DEMO DATA: Uncollapsed subterranean volcanic conduits and unweathered basalt fields provide structural analogs to lunar mare lava tubes and Marius Hills skylights.

name: Mauna Loa (HI-SEAS Station)
geology: Layered basalt shield lavas, pahoehoe corded ropes, cinder cones
surface_conditions: Loose basalt cinder, rough lava fields, low vegetative cover
recommended_missions: Crew Isolation and ECLSS Life-Support Stress Tests
Space Suit Ergonomics and Joint Seal Abrasion
explanation: DEMO DATA: Isolated high-altitude shield volcano environment suitable for crew operational autonomy, dust mitigation, and habitat life-support engineering.

name: Svalbard (Bockfjorden / AMASE Site)
terrain: Arctic volcanic complex and glaciated moraines
geology: Volcanic cones, carbonate globules, permafrost, mantle xenoliths
surface_conditions: Fractured permafrost bedrock, patterned gravel polygons, glacial outwash
explanation: DEMO DATA: Volcanic-glacial interactions and unique carbonate mineral precipitates structurally analogous to mineral signatures observed in Martian meteorites.

name: Wadi Rum (Valley of the Moon)
terrain: Deep sandstone canyons, inselbergs, and sand dunes
slope: 1° - 45° (Flat desert canyon floors to sheer sandstone cliffs)
geology: Iron-oxide enriched quartz sandstones, granite basement bedrock, aeolian sands
surface_conditions: Fine reddish sand dunes, hard bedrock pavements, steep canyon walls
recommended_missions: Rover Wheel Traction & Sand Dune Traversability
Optical SLAM Navigation in Iron-Oxide Landscapes
High-Heat Thermal Cycling on Mechanical Joints
explanation: DEMO DATA: Red iron-oxide sandstone morphology and sandy canyon floors replicate Martian canyon landscapes like Valles Marineris for autonomous rover navigation.

name: Corona Volcanic Cave System
terrain: Subterranean multi-level volcanic lava tube network
geology: Layered basaltic roof ceilings, lateral lava benches, pyrometasomatic minerals
surface_conditions: Enclosed dark basalt chambers, cave-ins, no solar illumination
recommended_missions: Underground Wireless Mesh Relays and Sensor Networks
explanation: DEMO DATA: A 6-km subterranean volcanic tube offering realistic conditions for testing human habitation concepts protected from cosmic radiation and meteoroids.

name: Mojave Desert (Pisgah Crater)
terrain: Basaltic volcanic cinder cone and surrounding lava field
geology: Porphyritic basalt, pahoehoe lava flows, vesicular scoria cinder
aridity: Arid Mojave desert (<100 mm annual precipitation)
surface_conditions: Rough basalt clinkers, abrasive volcanic cinders, dry desert pavement
recommended_missions: Steep Slope Rover Traction & Tipping Analysis
Abrasive Cinder Regolith Wear on Rover Wheels
Dust Penetration Testing on Seals and Gaskets
explanation: DEMO DATA: Highly abrasive cinder and basalt flows mimic young volcanic plains on the Moon and Mars for chassis traction and dust barrier testing.

name: Askja Caldera & Holuhraun
terrain: High volcanic plateau, caldera lake, and extensive flood basalts
geology: Flood basalts, hyaloclastites, pumice fields, geothermal fissure vents
aridity: Arid to semi-arid volcanic cold desert
surface_conditions: Fresh unweathered black basalt plains, pumice scree, snow-interbedded volcanic ash
recommended_missions: Geothermal Power & Subsurface Heat Flow Probes
explanation: DEMO DATA: Historic training ground for lunar geology due to vast unweathered basalt flows, caldera geometry, and sparse vegetation.

name: Danakil Depression (Dallol Geothermal Area)
terrain: Rift valley basin 120m below sea level with hydrothermal domes
geology: Hypersaline halite evaporites, sulfur chimneys, iron-rich hydrothermal springs
surface_conditions: Acidic salt crusts, toxic geothermal gases, hydrothermal brine pools
recommended_missions: Extreme Environment Robotics and Corrosion Testing
Extreme Thermal Stress Testing on Electronics
explanation: DEMO DATA: Hypersaline, acidic hydrothermal pools and sulfur-rich deposits simulate extreme geochemical niches that could have hosted life on early Mars.
